blockers.whatFailed: 3 patients have a stored Time-in-Range value that does not match the value recomputed from their raw CGM readings (for example Stored Time-in-Range 65.00% vs 80.54% recomputed from raw readings (difference 15.54pp)) — outside the configured 2-percentage-point tolerance. Check: device_derived_metric_consistency_cgm
blockers.whatUnlocks: Once governance confirms the accepted computation method, derived metrics like Time-in-Range become defensible, manufacturer-independent inputs to stratification and reporting.

blockers.whatFailed: 5 of 25 monitored patients have CGM device records that cannot be linked to their patient identity — the device stream carries a device ID that matches no patient on file. Check: device_patient_linkage_cgm
blockers.whatUnlocks: Once the vendor implements the device-to-patient ID crosswalk, these patients’ device streams become attributable and the weekly stratification review can include them on current device data.

blockers.whatFailed: 8 of 25 monitored patients have CGM coverage below the configured 70% floor over the 14-day review window — the gaps are too large for the data to support reliable glycemic review. Check: device_temporal_density_cgm_14d
blockers.whatUnlocks: Restored device coverage gives the care team a continuous signal they can trust, so these patients re-enter the weekly stratification review on current device data.

blockers.whatFailed: 3 of 36 diabetes patients have no A1C result inside the configured 6-month recency window — a value exists on record, but it is too old to reflect current control. Check: fitness_recency_a1c
blockers.whatUnlocks: A current A1C — lab collection at the next visit, or device enrollment so continuous glucose data carries current glycemic monitoring — restores an up-to-date picture of control for these patients’ weekly review.

blockers.whatFailed: 3 patients have an A1C value recorded outside the plausible clinical range of 2.0–20.0% (for example A1C 81.0 % (OBS000095) — outside the plausible 2–20 % range) — consistent with a unit or entry error at the source. Check: layer2_ranges_numeric_a1c
blockers.whatUnlocks: With plausible values restored, the A1C history becomes clinically usable and these patients’ glycemic picture can be trusted in review and reporting.

blockers.whatFailed: 4 patients have an A1C result whose date does not agree with the linked encounter’s recorded date (for example 1 of 7 A1C results discordant — OBS000134 resulted 2024-02-18 vs ENC000187 dated "02/18/2024") — the mismatch traces to a non-conformant encounter date, not the lab value. Check: layer5_date_concordance_a1c
blockers.whatUnlocks: A concordant result-date trail keeps the A1C history reliable for the review and reporting workflows that depend on when a value was actually drawn.

blockers.whatFailed: 6 of 35 hypertension patients have no smoking-status observation on record — a required variable for hypertension risk stratification was never captured at the point of care. Check: layer1_notnull_fields_smoking
blockers.whatUnlocks: Once smoking status is documented at the point of care, hypertension risk stratification can order the full panel for the weekly review instead of leaving these patients unscored.

blockers.whatFailed: 2 patients have condition records carrying codes that are not valid ICD-10 (for example Invalid ICD-10 code: E1X.21 (1 of 8 condition rows)) — malformed values, non-existent codes, or legacy ICD-9 remnants. Check: layer2_value_standards
blockers.whatUnlocks: Valid ICD-10 codes make the problem list exchangeable, unblocking care coordination on a diagnosis picture every participating system can read.

blockers.whatFailed: 3 patients have medication records carrying codes that are not valid RxNorm concepts (for example Invalid RxNorm code: 999999 (1 of 13 medication rows)) — malformed or placeholder values a receiving system cannot interpret. Check: layer3_mapped_values
blockers.whatUnlocks: Valid RxNorm codes make the medication list machine-readable across systems, unblocking care coordination on a medication picture every participating site can reconcile.

blockers.whatFailed: 3 patients have encounter records in the reporting window arriving with required structural fields empty (for example 1 of 5 in-window encounters malformed — ENC000395 missing class, provider_id) — the source feed is delivering malformed records. Check: layer1_notnull_fields_encounters
blockers.whatUnlocks: A correctly configured feed restores complete encounter records at the source, keeping clinical quality and value-based care reporting grounded in structurally sound data.

blockers.whatFailed: 6 patients have encounters whose recorded date does not agree with the dates on the clinical facts linked to them (for example 7 of 52 linked facts discordant — ENC000187 dated "02/18/2024" vs 7 linked facts at 2024-02-18) — non-conformant formats or transposed values in the encounter date. Check: layer5_date_concordance
blockers.whatUnlocks: Conformant encounter dates make the encounter record trustworthy for clinical quality and value-based care reporting — the downstream half of the care model that runs on EHR data.

criteria.label: CGM temporal density ≥ 0.70 over the 14-day window
Time-in-Range recomputation tolerance ± 2pp against raw readings
A1C recency: 6-month lookback from the evaluation date
Site-level display band: PARTIALLY_READY ≥ 0.85 of population READY

pipeline.label: Ingest
pipeline.description: Raw EHR and device extracts land in the staging tier exactly as delivered — nothing is altered on arrival.

pipeline.label: Parse
pipeline.description: Records are read against the expected structure; malformed records are identified at the earliest possible point and traced to their source feed.

pipeline.label: Normalize
pipeline.description: Values are standardized into the shared model; unambiguous corrections can be AI-assisted, with a human approving every change.

pipeline.label: Score
pipeline.description: The deterministic core: every check, variable, and pathway is evaluated against the configured criteria — same inputs, same results, every time.

pipeline.label: Readiness report
pipeline.description: Results are organized per use case: what is ready, what is blocked, and exactly why.

pipeline.label: Remediate
pipeline.description: Each blocker is routed to the role that can fix it; where an AI-suggested fix applies, it waits for human approval.

pipeline.label: Re-score
pipeline.description: Remediated data goes back through the same deterministic scoring path, and the readiness report is refreshed from the stored results.

pipeline.label: Unlock
pipeline.description: Use cases whose criteria are met come online — the weekly stratification review and downstream reporting run on data that is fit for purpose.
